lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Saturday, ten a.m.: the **Great Singapore Sale** at Plaza Seratus.
**Mum:** Listen up. Budget: **$200**. Rule one: **never pay full price**.
**Dad:** I'll give it **a hundred and ten per cent**!
**Kavya:** Dad. A hundred per cent is **everything**. You can't give more.
**Ah Boy:** Look! **50% off**, then **another 20% off**! That's **70% off**!
**Narrator:** But this documentary is about the tiny sign on every banner in the mall.
**Percy:** Percy! The **per cent sign**! Per cent means **out of a hundred**!
**Percy:** A slash and two zeros. Basically a **100** that fell over.
**Percy:** My great-great-grandad: the Italian **per cento**, 'for each hundred'. Merchants scribbled him smaller.
**Percy:** I rate everything **out of a hundred**. Seventy per cent off? I give that a **twelve**.
**Percy:** One family. Two hundred dollars. Let's play...
**Narrator:** Out of a Hundred. Episode 6: The Great Singapore Sale.
**Narrator:** Ten fifteen. Three rival shops. Three very different signs.
**Priya:** Priya. Bargain expert. **62% off** wins. Biggest number!
**Percy:** Different forms! Put them all in the **same form** first.
**Kavya:** So **0.6 < 62% < ⅝**. The **fraction** shop wins!
**Percy:** Decimal to per cent: **× 100**. Back: **÷ 100**, so **35% = 0.35**. As a fraction: **35/100 = 7/20**.
**Kavya:** Or scale the bottom up to 100: **7/25 = 28/100 = 28%**.
**Ah Boy:** That one says **0.5% cashback**. I get **half** my money back!
**Percy:** **0.5%** is **half of one per cent**: **0.005**. Spend **$10**, get back **5 cents**.
**Dad:** And I'm **still** giving it a hundred and ten per cent.
**Kavya:** Dad. That's **impossible**.
**Percy:** Wrong! **100%** is **one whole**. **110%** is just **1.1**: a whole, plus a tenth.
**Dad:** Hear that? I'm **one point one** dads.
**Kavya:** One dad is plenty.
**Narrator:** Eleven a.m. The shoe shop. Ah Boy needs new school shoes.
**Ah Boy:** These are **$64**, and **15% off**! How much do we save?
**Tenner:** I'm Tenner! **10%**! That's **divide by ten**!
**Tenner:** My little brother **Fiver**. **5%** is **half** of me: **$3.20**.
**Mum:** We pay 64 − 9.60 = **$54.40**. **Never** pay full price.
**Percy:** Bonus: **x% of y = y% of x**. **4% of 25**? Swap: **25% of 4** = **1**!
**Dad:** Blender, **$260**, **37% off**. Calculator time.
**Percy:** 'Of' means **times**. Use a decimal: **0.37 × 260 = 96.2**.
**Dad:** Ninety-six dollars and... two cents?
**Kavya:** **$96.20**. Money always gets **two decimal places**.
**Percy:** **Estimate**: 37% is about a **third**. A third of 260: about **87**. Believable.
**Tenner:** Ten, five, one. Every morning. Before breakfast.
**Narrator:** Twelve noon. The bookshop. Kavya's maths teacher, **Mr Tan**, is buying red pens. In bulk.
**Mr Tan:** I marked your tests on the MRT. Kavya: **18 out of 24**. Priya: **21 out of 30**.
**Priya:** **21** is more than **18**. I win.
**Percy:** Different totals! Rescale both to **out of a hundred**.
**Mr Tan:** Percentage = **part ÷ whole × 100**. The **whole**, after 'out of', goes on the **bottom**.
**Priya:** I demand a recount.
**Mr Tan:** Tests are like the sale. Some of you got **marked down**.
**Ah Boy:** I spent **45 cents** of my **$2** on sweets. 45 ÷ 2 × 100... **2250%**!
**Percy:** Mr Tan's joke? **Four** out of a hundred.
**Narrator:** One p.m. The electronics shop. '**Tomorrow, all prices up 15%**'.
**Dad:** Rice cooker, **$40**. 15% of 40 is **$6**. Add it on: **$46**. Two steps.
**The Great Multiplini:** Two steps? How... **ordinary**. The Great Multiplini does it in **ONE**.
**The Great Multiplini:** Start at **100%**. Add 15%: **115%**. That's **1.15**. Behold: **40 × 1.15 = $46**! Ta-da!
**Kavya:** Same thing: **40 + 0.15 × 40 = 40 × 1.15**. One number, **both** steps.
**The Great Multiplini:** **Increase** by r%: × **(1 + r/100)**. **Decrease**: × **(1 − r/100)**.
**Ah Boy:** My turn! The kettle goes up **5%**! Multiply by **1.5**!
**The Great Multiplini:** Above **1**: **increase**. Below **1**: **decrease**. **× 0.93** is **7% off**.
**The Great Multiplini:** And **9% GST**? **× 1.09**. A **$50** kettle costs 50 × 1.09 = **$54.50**.
**Percy:** Magic: ninety. The cape: a **hundred**.

chapters.title: A dollar on the kaya toast

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Two p.m. The food court. Mum reads the menu, and gasps.
**Mum:** Kaya toast set! **$4** last year. Now **$5**! Up a whole dollar!
**Dad:** Relax. My bike went from **$250** to **$251**. Also a dollar. Same same.
**Olive:** Excuse me. **Olive**. The **original price**. Everyone crosses me out. But **I'm the whole**.
**Olive:** **Absolute change** = new − original: **$1** each. Now compare it with **me**.
**Kavya:** Toast: 1/4 × 100 = **25%**. Bike: 1/250 × 100 = **0.4%**. Same dollar. Very different change.
**Olive:** **Percentage change = change ÷ original × 100**. **New minus Old, over Old.**
**Ah Boy:** But $1 out of the **new** price, **$5**, is **20%**!
**Olive:** **Wrong whole!** Divide by the **original**, $4. Never the new price. It's **25%**.
**Olive:** Or divide **new by original**: 5 ÷ 4 = **1.25**. Up **25%**.
**Dad:** News: '**Otter sightings up 300%!**' Last year, **5**. So now, **15**.
**Olive:** Up **300%** means **400%** of the original: **× 4**. 5 × 4 = **20** sightings. **15 more**.
**Kavya:** And **GST** went from **8%** to **9%**. That's up **1 percentage point**, but **1/8** more tax: **12.5%**!
**Mum:** Either way, my toast still costs five dollars.
**Narrator:** Three p.m. Mum finds **the** jacket. Already **20% off**: **$48**.
**Mum:** I need the **original** price. For bragging.
**Olive:** **Wrong whole!** The 20% came off **me**, the **original**. Not off the sale price!
**The Great Multiplini:** Or in **one** step: undo my trick. **Divide** by the multiplier: 48 ÷ 0.8 = **$60**. Ad-aT!
**Olive:** **Original = new amount ÷ multiplier**. Going back? **Divide, don't subtract.**
**Mum:** I saved **$12**. Priya, I'm telling everyone.
**Kavya:** This receipt: **$43.60**, **including 9% GST**. What was it **before** GST?
**Priya:** Easy! Take **9%** off: **$39.68**!
**Olive:** Wrong whole! **Again!** The 9% was 9% of the price **before** GST.
**Priya:** I demand a recount.
**Narrator:** Four p.m. The bank. Ah Boy has **$500** of ang bao money.
**Priya:** I'm a businesswoman. Bought an old bike for **$150**, sold it for **$186**.
**Percy:** Profit: 186 − 150 = **$36**. Profit % is out of the **cost price**: 36/150 × 100 = **24%**.
**Ah Boy:** If I save my **$500** at **3%** simple interest a year, how much after **4 years**?
**Kavya:** **$15** every year. After 4 years: 500 + 60 = **$560**.
**Snowy:** Ho ho! **Snowy**! **Compound interest**! I earn interest on my **interest**!
**Kavya:** Simple interest adds the same **amount** each year. Snowy adds the same **percentage**.
**Ah Boy:** So **10% up**, then **10% down**, gets you back to the start!
**Olive:** Wrong whole! **$100** up 10% is **$110**. 10% **of 110** is **$11**. You're left with **$99**.
**Snowy:** Changes in a row? **Multiply the multipliers**: × 1.1 × 0.9 = **× 0.99**. A **1%** loss.
**Kavya:** So Ah Boy's banner: × 0.5 × 0.8 = **× 0.4**. You pay **40%**. That's **60% off**, not seventy.
**Ah Boy:** Fine. **$10** at **2%** compound. I'll wait to be a millionaire.
**Snowy:** That takes about **582 years**.
**Ah Boy:** I can wait.

chapters.title: The mall saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits, the mall would like to save you some marks.
**Olive:** One. Percentage change: divide by the **original**. Never by the new value.
**The Great Multiplini:** Two. Going back? **Divide** by the multiplier. Never add the percentage back on.
**Ah Boy:** Three. **7%** is **0.07**, not 0.7. **0.5%** is **0.005**. Not half. I checked.
**Mr Tan:** Four. **Same units** first. Cents with cents. Red pens with red pens.
**Mum:** Five. **Reread the last line**: do they want the **discount**, or the **price you pay**?
**Dad:** Six. **25% off** then **9% GST** is **not 16% off**. Multiply: **× 0.75 × 1.09**.
**Narrator:** Out of a Hundred will return.
**Narrator:** Six p.m. The car park. Mum checks the receipts.
**Mum:** Total spent: **$220**. Our budget was **$200**.
**Dad:** I told you. I gave it **a hundred and ten per cent**.
**Kavya:** 220 ÷ 200 × 100 = **110%**. Dad. You **spent** a hundred and ten per cent.
**Percy:** Over a hundred per cent: **totally allowed**. Totally **his fault**.
